articles.headline: CISA says it had to build its incident playbook during a live cybersecurity event
articles.summary: TechCrunch reports that the U.S. cybersecurity agency CISA had to develop parts of its incident response playbook while the incident was still unfolding. For businesses, the key implication is that public-sector cyber readiness remains uneven, reinforcing the need for stronger internal response plans and vendor controls.

articles.headline: Meta to start producing its own AI chip in September, aiming to double computing capacity
articles.summary: Meta plans to begin manufacturing an in-house AI chip in September as part of a broader push to expand computing capacity. For businesses, this signals continued pressure on AI infrastructure demand and a race to secure cheaper, more controllable compute for large-scale AI deployment.

articles.headline: Microsoft strikes a multibillion-dollar compute deal with Mistral
articles.summary: Microsoft reached a multibillion-dollar deal to rent AI infrastructure from Mistral, underscoring how quickly demand for compute capacity is becoming a strategic enterprise issue. The deal matters for business leaders because it reflects the rising cost and importance of AI infrastructure, especially for firms evaluating cloud spending and vendor dependence.
